text: Which AWS service uses machine learning and pattern matching to discover personally identifiable information stored in Amazon S3 buckets?
explanation: Amazon Macie discovers sensitive data such as PII in Amazon S3 and also flags buckets that are public or shared. GuardDuty detects threats from activity logs, and Inspector scans workloads for software vulnerabilities; neither inspects the content of S3 objects for PII.

text: An application running on an Amazon EC2 instance must read objects from an Amazon S3 bucket. What is the MOST secure way to give the application this access?

options.text: Store an IAM user's access keys in a configuration file on the instance
Attach an IAM role that allows reading the bucket to the instance
Use the access keys of the AWS account root user in the application
Use an S3 gateway VPC endpoint

explanation: An IAM role attached to the instance delivers temporary credentials that rotate automatically, so no long-term secrets are stored on the instance. Access keys in a file are long-term credentials that keep working if they leak, and an S3 gateway VPC endpoint only provides a private network path; it does not give the application any permissions.

text: A company has a standalone AWS account that is not part of AWS Organizations. Which tasks require signing in with the AWS account root user credentials? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create an IAM user group for developers
View the monthly bill in the Billing console
Edit an Amazon S3 bucket policy that denies all principals
Launch an Amazon EC2 instance in a new Region

explanation: Closing a standalone account and fixing an S3 bucket policy that denies every principal are tasks that require the root user. IAM identities with the right permissions can create groups and launch instances, and they can view bills once the root user has activated IAM access to the Billing console.

text: An IAM user has an identity-based policy that allows s3:DeleteObject on a bucket. The bucket policy contains a statement that explicitly denies s3:DeleteObject for that user. What happens when the user tries to delete an object?

options.text: The request is allowed because identity-based policies are evaluated first
The request is denied because an explicit deny overrides any allow
The request is allowed only if the user signed in with MFA
The result depends on which policy was created most recently

explanation: AWS evaluates all applicable policies together, and an explicit Deny in any of them overrides every Allow. Order of evaluation or creation date does not change the result.

text: A company uses AWS Organizations with 40 AWS accounts. Employees should sign in once with their existing corporate directory credentials and then choose the account and permissions they need. Which AWS service should the company use?

options.text: Separate IAM users in each account

explanation: IAM Identity Center gives the workforce single sign-on to multiple AWS accounts and can connect to an existing identity provider. Amazon Cognito is meant for the customers who use your own web and mobile applications, not for employee access to AWS accounts.

text: A company is building a mobile app for consumers. Users must be able to sign up, sign in, and optionally sign in with their Google accounts. Which AWS service provides this functionality?

options.text: AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) users

explanation: Amazon Cognito user pools provide sign-up and sign-in for web and mobile app users, including social identity providers such as Google. IAM Identity Center is for workforce access to AWS accounts and business applications, and IAM users are not meant for an app's end users.

text: A developer stores a database password in the source code of an application. The security team wants the password removed from the code and changed automatically on a regular schedule. Which AWS service should the developer use?
explanation: Secrets Manager stores secrets such as database credentials, lets applications retrieve them at runtime, and can rotate them automatically. AWS KMS manages encryption keys; it does not store and rotate application passwords.

text: A company runs a public web application behind an Application Load Balancer. It must block SQL injection attempts and wants expanded DDoS protection with access to AWS DDoS response experts. Which AWS services meet these requirements? (Choose two.)
explanation: AWS WAF filters HTTP(S) requests with rules that can block SQL injection, and Shield Advanced adds expanded DDoS protection and access to the Shield Response Team. GuardDuty detects threats but does not block requests, and Inspector and Macie scan for vulnerabilities and sensitive data.

text: A security team needs a service that analyzes AWS CloudTrail events, VPC flow logs, and DNS logs to detect threats such as compromised credentials and communication with known malicious IP addresses. Which service meets this need?
explanation: Amazon GuardDuty is a threat detection service that analyzes these log sources with threat intelligence and machine learning. Amazon Inspector looks for software vulnerabilities in workloads, and AWS Config records resource configurations rather than detecting threats.

text: Which statements about AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) keys are correct? (Choose two.)

options.text: Customer managed keys let the customer define the key policy
Customers can schedule AWS managed keys for deletion
AWS managed keys are rotated automatically every year
Customer managed keys have no monthly charge
AWS owned keys can be viewed in the customer's KMS console

explanation: With customer managed keys the customer controls the key policy, rotation and deletion, and AWS KMS rotates AWS managed keys automatically every year. Customers cannot delete AWS managed keys, customer managed keys have a monthly fee, and AWS owned keys are not visible in the customer's account.
